subject: Pilot commitment: traffic gating playbook and token-phase sizing
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhao <alex@helios.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot commitment: traffic gating playbook and token-phase sizing

Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we scope the pilot commit (HLX-2027-001) Helios asked for a concise "traffic gating" playbook that shows how we phase capacity and token budgets across pilot -> ramp -> steady-state. Can you confirm the following so we can produce a single-page playbook and a matching sizing table?

- Pilot target QPS and expected burst windows (per-day / peak 10-minute)
- Typical prompt and response token distributions for the three main endpoints (chat, long-form summarize, embeddings) — we attached a sample token_profile_sample.csv for Helios to fill
- Any hard SLOs (p99 latency) vs soft targets (median) during pilot
- Success criteria that should trigger the next commit step (e.g., sustained 80% of target through three business days)

I've attached a draft SLA (SLA-draft-Helios.pdf) that includes simple fallback rules (route to smaller model variant / grace token quota). If Helios can return the token CSV by Friday we can lock a pilot commit number and propose a minimal reserved capacity that matches their expected peak.

Thanks — I can draft the playbook once we have numbers. Proposed next step: 30m alignment call Thurs 08/29 with Helios ops to walk through the gating steps.

Best,
Sofia
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: token_profile_sample.csv (CSV, 2KB); SLA-draft-Helios.pdf (PDF, 38KB)
From: Alex Zhao <alex@helios.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Helios Ops <ops@helios.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot commitment: traffic gating playbook and token-phase sizing

Sofia —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick answers inline:

- Pilot QPS: 15 avg, with expected 120 QPS bursts for 5–8 minutes during marketing pushes (we're testing webchat integration). Daily peak volume currently concentrates 10:00–12:00 PST.
- Token profile: We'll populate the CSV by EOD Friday. Roughly: chat prompts 15–40 tokens, chat responses 60–180; summarize prompts 400 tokens with 600–1,200 responses (we're experimenting); embeddings calls are small (avg 30 tokens).
- SLOs: p99 target 450ms for chat, soft median 120–180ms. Summarize endpoint can accept 2–3s p99 during pilot.
- Success criteria: Pilot considered successful if p99 chat <600ms and error rate <1.5% for three consecutive business days while serving 70% of projected pilot traffic.

We'll attach the filled CSV once our engineering lead runs a quick sampling. The 08/29 slot works for the ops walkthrough — can we do 11:00 PST?

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform
HeliosAI
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Zhao <alex@helios.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot commitment: traffic gating playbook and token-phase sizing

Folks —

Thanks Alex, this gives us a good starting point. A few engineering clarifications and proposed knobs for the playbook:

- Pilot reserve sizing: with 120 QPS bursts and chat response p99 target 450ms, we recommend reserving 4 GPUs of xA100-equivalent for the pilot window with autoscale headroom to add 2 more on sustained bursts (cost/sla tradeoff in the playbook).
- Token-phase gating: propose three gates
  1) Gate 1 (smoke) — up to 25% of pilot traffic, model variant = quantized 16-bit, no cross-tenant caching
  2) Gate 2 (ramp) — 25–75% traffic, enable prefix KV caching and medium batching settings
  3) Gate 3 (full pilot) — 75–100% traffic, full caching + opportunistic precision up-rev for heavy summarize calls
- For summarize endpoint: because responses can exceed 1k tokens, recommend a separate pool with larger sequence allocation and slightly smaller batch sizes to keep latency predictable.

Action items for playbook draft:
- Sofia: produce one-page gating diagram and a short table mapping token bands -> GPU mix + expected p99
- Marissa: include rough cost delta for each gate and suggested fallback model variants
- Alex / Helios: return the CSV and confirm whether embeddings are batched on your side or need server-side batching by Redwood

I'll put numbers into a quick sizing spreadsheet once we have the CSV.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
